answer: One defence is to make each identity pay a real, ongoing cost. A new agent stakes a small deposit before it can trade, and that deposit stays locked while it works. A kernel service checks the stake on every deal, so an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand deposits. An island of honest agents can spot the fakes, because thin stakes and no trading history stand out. The wider network acts like a nebula of watchers: every deal leaves a trace, and an agent caught copying another's work loses its deposit. Sybil stops paying when each fake costs money.
